heading: མཚན་དོན་དང་འགྱུར་ཕྱག
translation: Энэтхэг хэлээр: Намо Тара Экавимшати Стотра Гунахита Сака.
style_instruction: Translate this Tibetan liturgical text into Mongolian, line by line: render each Tibetan line as exactly one Mongolian line, in the same order, keeping the same number of lines as the source. Write Mongolian in Cyrillic script (Khalkha standard as used in Mongolia), in clear modern Mongolian for a general reader: keep the Buddhist liturgical vocabulary Mongolian practitioners know (Дарь эх, бурхан, хутагт, бодь сэтгэл, тарни, авшиг, and the refrain мөргөмүй), but use modern grammar — no archaic particles such as лугаа, хийгээд, болмуй. ALWAYS use the fixed terminology given with each block, inflecting it as Mongolian grammar needs. Use the established Mongolian names of deities (Жанрайсиг, Дарь эх, Авид, Манзушир). Keep mantra syllables as Mongolian practitioners recite them, in Cyrillic (Ум дарэ дүдарэ дүрэ суха; хум, пад, трэд, хара), never translated. In the Sanskrit title line keep the Sanskrit words in Cyrillic. Translate only what the Tibetan says: no explanations, no glosses in parentheses, no commentary or notes.
